description:
Filed by s527b (2026-10-29) from the corpus-diff of 072a105e.  perl-tests/hashassign.t:518 `$_++ foreach sub :lvalue { %h = ($x,$x) }->();`: on main PPI mis-lexed `sub :` as a label, Pl::Parser2::_normalize_anon_sub_attrs turned it back into `sub { … }` (dropping :lvalue) and the capture pass marked $x `:captured t`; with PCL's PPI the attribute stays and the ordinary attributed-anon-sub path wraps the sub in (p-__pcl_set_attributes …) -- and $x's p-let binding no longer carries `:captured t`.  The ordinary path never set it: on MAIN `my @s; for my $i (1..2) { my $x = $i; push @s, sub :lvalue { $x } }` emits no `:captured` either.  So the capture scanner does not look through an anon sub's Attribute tokens (it skips Prototype / Signature only -- compare _cond_mys_closure_captured's #3368 R9 note).

Probes (perl / tree / main): the hashassign.t row gives x=0 all three; the loop closure prints 12 all three -- no behavioural difference found.  The bar for the fix: find a program whose output depends on the flag (a closure created in a loop body that outlives the iteration and mutates the captured cell), probe it perl vs tree, then teach the scanner to skip Attribute tokens (ONE place: grep the capture scanner for its Prototype/Signature skip).


=== s527b (s530): READ AS PRE-EXISTING ===
Probe scratch/s527b/p3943.pl (worktree agent-a743b493df5814081): a loop closure over `sub :lvalue { $x }` and over `sub :prototype() { $y++ }` -- the s527b tree and main print the same (and the :lvalue one emits no `:captured t` on main either: the ordinary attributed-anon-sub path never sets it).  The `.=` through the lvalue closure differs from perl on BOTH (#930, lvalue subs deferred).  So s527b's group S only MOVED perl-tests/hashassign.t:518 onto the ordinary path; the missing mark is the path's, not the batch's.  No behavioural difference found yet; the bar in the description stands.
subject: An anonymous sub WITH ATTRIBUTES (sub :lvalue { $x }) is not marked as capturing: its captured lexicals lose `:captured t` (no behavioural difference found yet)
